display.purpose: The name on the intro panel, two stacked lines sized to the panel.

headline.purpose: One screen title per screen; on the plan it states the result.

action.purpose: The word on the Start tag only.

name.purpose: Wordmark in the bar, the Contracts heading, each ticket's market name.

figure.purpose: Crop value at the foot of the farm tag and the order total.

stamp.purpose: Red stamps: the place name, Sample, Demo only.

promise.purpose: The single sentence under the name.

lede.purpose: The sentence under the plan title.

label.purpose: Form questions, button text, table values.

note.purpose: Hints, units, fine print, axis labels.

shadows.name: tooltip-lift
shadows.purpose: The chart tooltip only, the one element that floats over other content.

shadows.name: thumb-lift
shadows.purpose: The slider thumb, so it reads as the grabbable part of the track.

shadows.name: eyelet-ring
shadows.purpose: A hard ring, not a shadow: the reinforcement around a tag's punched hole (5px on the Start tag).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one curve for every move: pin, line, stamp, screens, presses, chart columns.

motion.name: screen-in
motion.purpose: A screen rising in. Reduced motion: 160ms fade.

motion.name: pin-drop
motion.purpose: The pin landing on the map. Reduced motion: 150ms fade in place.

motion.name: landing-ring
motion.value: 280ms after a 200ms delay, scale 0.5 to 3.4, opacity 0.75 to 0
motion.purpose: The red ring that marks where the pin landed; the one move longer than 300ms. Not played under reduced motion.

motion.name: station-line
motion.purpose: The line running from the pin to the nearest station; its label fades in over 160ms at 420ms.

motion.name: stamp-press
motion.value: 180ms after a 230ms delay, rotate(-2deg) scale(1.16) and opacity 0 to rotate(-2deg) scale(1)
motion.purpose: The place name stamped onto the tag just after the pin lands. Reduced motion: fade only.

motion.name: state-change
motion.value: 150ms ease on background-color, border-color and color
motion.purpose: Hover, selection and the yellow flood of the focused row.

motion.name: press
motion.value: 120ms, scale(0.97); 140ms, scale(0.98) on the Start tag
motion.purpose: Buttons and Yes and No sides giving under the pointer.

motion.name: column-move
motion.purpose: Chart columns and the budget meter moving to new values.

narrative.overview:
Farmer Joe is a brand printed on a seed sack. The intro is the front of the sack: a corn-yellow panel that runs edge to edge with the name in capitals as tall as the panel allows. The farm form is the sack's tag, filled in one ruled row at a time while a yellow map answers. The plan reads like the analysis tag sewn to a bag: a title that states the result, ruled figures, and contracts as tickets. Farmer Joe is the product's name only; nothing on screen speaks as a character.

Everything is flat print. There are three inks (sack green, corn yellow, tag red) and one stock (white tag card). Green is the ground of every screen, so the white tags are objects sitting on it, never a page behind them. Density is that of a filled-in form: 15px reading text, 10px row padding, rules instead of boxes. The system refuses the white onboarding wizard of progress bar and rounded cards.

Motion is things landing and pressing. The pin drops onto the map (260ms) and a red ring spreads from the landing point, a line runs out to the nearest station (280ms), and the place name is stamped onto the tag's first row (180ms, scaling down from 1.16 at its 2 degree tilt). Screens rise in 18px over 240ms. Every move shares one curve, `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`; state changes on controls take 120 to 200ms. The one longer piece is the landing ring, which fades over 460ms. Under reduced motion the pin and stamp fade in place, screens cross-fade in 160ms, and transitions are cut to nothing.

The finish review left four ideas open that are not in the build and are not part of this system yet: seam or lot devices on the sack front, eyelets and perforations on the plan's tags, a tag-pull screen change, and ruled rows under the map.
keyCharacteristics: Sack green is the ground of all three screens; white appears only as tag stock and as type on green.
Corn yellow marks one thing per region: the panel, the current step, the row being answered, the contract that is in the plan.
Heavy condensed capitals for the name, screen titles and key figures; a plain grotesque for everything read or operated.
Data sits in ruled rows, label left and value right, opened by a 2px ink rule and separated by 1px hairlines.
One chart form: two distributions stacked on a shared ruled grid, in two greens.
Sample and demo data is stamped in red, tilted 2 degrees.

rules.name: The Green Ground Rule
rules.body: Every screen's background is sack green. White never becomes the page; it is always a tag, a ticket or a field sitting on the green.

rules.name: The Yellow Means Chosen Rule
rules.body: Yellow is a flood, never a tint or an outline, and outside the intro panel and the map it marks exactly one current thing per region: the step you are on, the row you are answering, the contract you have picked. Yellow is never text on tag stock and is not used in the chart, because it cannot hold contrast there.

rules.name: The Red Is Pressed On Rule
rules.body: Red is for the pin, the stamps, warnings, and No. It never decorates and never fills a surface larger than a button.

rules.name: The Yes And No Rule
rules.body: Yes prints in green and No prints in red, tinted at rest and solid when pressed. The word is always printed beside the colour, so the pair never depends on hue alone.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Big Shoulders is for the name, screen titles, market names, key figures and stamps, always at 800 or 900 and never below 15px. Anything the farmer reads as a sentence or operates as a control is Archivo.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change or be compared (prices, amounts, table cells, axis ticks, field values) uses tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Printed Flat Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are separated by ink and stock, never by shadow. A shadow is allowed only on something that floats above the print (the tooltip) or is physically grabbed (the slider thumb).

dos: Do put every screen on sack green (`green-700`) and keep white for tags, tickets, fields and type on green.
Do flood with yellow to show the one current or chosen thing in a region: the step, the focused row, the picked ticket.
Do set data as ruled rows, label left and value right, with a 2px ink rule opening the group and 1px `rule` hairlines between rows.
Do use Big Shoulders at 800 or 900 in capitals for the name, screen titles, market names, key figures and stamps, and Archivo for everything else.
Do print Yes in green and No in red with the word beside the colour, tinted at rest and solid when pressed.
Do stamp sample and demo data in red beside its heading, and keep the stamp's 2 degree tilt.
Do draw charts as two stacked bands on one shared ruled grid, `green-300` without protection and `green-700` with the plan.
Do keep moves on `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)` at 120 to 280ms, and give each one a fade-only fallback under reduced motion.
Do use tabular numerals for every price, amount and table figure.
donts: Don't make white the page background or lay tags out as a white wizard with a progress bar and rounded cards.
Don't use yellow in the chart or as text on tag stock; it cannot hold contrast there.
Don't use red for decoration or for any surface larger than a button; it is the pin, the stamps, warnings and No.
Don't add a fourth ink. Neutrals come from the green (`ink`, `ink-2`, `ink-3`, `rule`, `rule-strong`, `tag-2`).
Don't add shadows to tags, tickets or buttons; only the chart tooltip and the slider thumb have one.
Don't round corners past 3px; circles are for eyelets, step numerals, dots and thumbs.
Don't write as Farmer Joe. It is the product's name, not a speaking character.
Don't show a sample or assumed number without its label.
